**Other information:**

## What the guard does now

`findUnnamedImages(packedPaths, readTextFile, {baseline})` is the second pure predicate beside
`findForbiddenEntries`. It collects every `folder/file.ext` token that appears in a packed text file
(`mjs`, `js`, `json`, `scss`, `css`, `md`, `html`, `yaml`, `yml`, `txt`, `svg`), then reports every
packed image (`png`, `jpg`, `jpeg`, `gif`, `webp`) whose own `folder/file.ext` is not in that set. The
match is on the last two segments, so `preview/dark.png` is found while `dark.png` occurs elsewhere. The
entry block calls it after the forbidden-prefix check; a finding fails the check and the message carries
the pinned-link rule verbatim.

## The count under the folder-and-name match

Measured on this branch's own `npm pack --dry-run --json`: **1014 packed images**, of which **420 match
no packed text file by folder and file name** (the bare-name table in the issue said 415 — the extra
five are frames whose bare name occurs in an unrelated folder):

| Folder | Files | Bytes | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| `resources/examples/ai_images/` | 399 | 5.29 MiB | **listed** — folder prefix, see below |
| `apps/portal/resources/images/team/` | 4 | 1.35 MiB | **referenced** — `picture: 'Max.jpeg'` beside the folder constant in `apps/portal/view/about/Container.mjs`; listed as a prefix |
| `resources/images/circle/` | 3 | <1 KiB | **referenced** — `itemFile = ['flip.png', 'pencil.png', 'trash.png']` in `src/component/Circle.mjs`; listed as a prefix |
| `test/playwright/visual/__screenshots__/` | 6 | 0.13 MiB | **referenced** — `snapshotPathTemplate: '{testDir}/__screenshots__/{testFileName}/{arg}{ext}'`, specs name only `{arg}`; listed as a prefix |
| `docs/resources/images/tutorials/` | 4 | 0.13 MiB | **listed** — orphaned: no packed text file names them. Kept, because the tutorial page that used them may be built outside this tree |
| `apps/portal/resources/images/examples/devmode/` | 2 | 0.48 MiB | **listed** — orphaned: `apps/portal/resources/data/examples.json` names `devmode/workstation-13-2.jpg` and `devmode/DevIndex.png`, not these two |
| `examples/component/process/realWorldExample/` | 1 | 0.60 MiB | **referenced** — `src: './RangeHeader.jpg'`, relative to its own folder, so no parent directory is in the reference |
| `resources/images/readme/` | 1 | 0.29 MiB | **listed** — orphaned poster |
| `examples/scheduler/basic/preview/` | 6 | 0.19 MiB | **removed** |

`resources/examples/ai_images/` holds **989** frames and `resources/examples/data/ai_contacts.json` names
**590** of them as `ai_images/<id>.jpg`; the remaining **399** are not named anywhere. The folder is read
by pattern, so it is baselined as a prefix with that count and that reason, and which frames a record set
uses is not something the tree can tell the guard.

The baseline is `buildScripts/util/check-package-contents-baseline.json`, 12 entries: 4 folder prefixes
and 8 single paths, each with its reason. A spec case asserts every entry names a `path` or a `prefix`
and states why, in the manner of the `FORBIDDEN_PREFIXES` case.

## The six frames

`git ls-files examples/scheduler/basic/preview` prints nothing on this branch, and every frame in the
description of #20888 still loads from its pinned commit (`curl -L` → 200, 33–65 KB each):

```
.../blob/0094fde13768adc228b671b9501be6a747d73502/examples/scheduler/basic/preview/dark.png?raw=true       200
.../light.png       200     .../dark-drag.png   200     .../dark-hour.png   200
.../light-drag.png  200     .../light-hour.png  200
```

## Red and green

Green on this branch: the predicate over this branch's real pack report returns **0** findings outside
the baseline.

Red with one planted file: `examples/scheduler/basic/planted-frame.png` (70 B) added, repacked, and the
same predicate returns exactly **1** finding:

```
examples/scheduler/basic/planted-frame.png
```

Both runs call the same two functions the entry block calls, over the real `npm pack --json` output.
`node buildScripts/util/check-package-contents.mjs` itself cannot run on this machine: `execFileSync('npm', …)`
resolves nothing on Windows (`ENOENT`), identically at the parent commit on `dev` — the three existing
spec cases that spawn `npm` fail the same way here, before and after this change. CI runs the script
itself on Linux, where the `package contents` step of `pr-baseline` exercises it.

`npx playwright test -c test/playwright/playwright.config.unit.mjs test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/checkPackageContents.spec.mjs --grep "packed image needs a reference|pack report is read"` → **12 passed**. The spec cases are the four the acceptance criteria name, plus the unreadable-reader case, the root-level key, the baseline-reason case and the rule-text case.

## One thing outside the ticket's letter, in service of it

`parsePackOutput` accepted only the array shape. npm 12.2.2 reports the payload as an **object keyed by
package name** (`{"neo.mjs": {…}}`), so the entry block threw `no JSON array found` on a current npm
before either predicate could run — which would have made the red/green evidence above unobtainable and
the new guard inert on any modern machine. The function now reads either shape: the payload is the first line that opens an array or an object, and a
lifecycle line that opens one of its own reds the gate. Three spec cases cover the shapes. If you would
rather see that as its own PR, say so and I will split it out.

## Out of scope, as the issue states

The 10.9 MB of named images and whether the 399 `ai_images` should ship at all. The orphaned single
files are listed rather than deleted: removing an app's stale frame or a doc image is a content
decision, not a guard's, and a second PR can do exactly that without arguing about the rule.

### `@iruzen-dono` commented on 2026-11-15T14:25:26Z

All four actions are in `e54a671`. Point by point, and one thing I found while doing RA-1 that belongs in this thread.

### RA-1 — the baseline now ratchets both ways

You were right, and the older sibling is the one I should have read: `diffAgainstBaseline` → `burnedDown` in `check-class-module-scope`, "The ratchet is symmetric" in its own words, and four more entries in `buildScripts/util/` doing the same. I built a one-way ratchet because the ticket pointed at the sibling's JSON, not its script — that is the `[KB_GAP]` you filed, and it is a real trap.

The predicate splits in two so the diff never re-reads the pack:

- `collectUnnamedImages(packedPaths, readTextFile)` → live unnamed images.
- `diffImageBaseline(unnamedImages, baseline)` → `{added, stale}`, mirroring `diffAgainstBaseline`.

`stale` fails the check with its own message and its own list — path or prefix, each with the reason it recorded — and the entry block reports `added` and `stale` in the same run, so a rename does not need two rounds. The spec covers both kinds you named: a `path` entry whose frame is unpacked or deleted, a `path` entry whose frame is now named by folder and file name, and a `prefix` entry that covers no unnamed image.

### The thing I found while proving RA-1

The spec itself was weakening the guard. `checkPackageContents.spec.mjs` is a **packed text file**, and its fixtures carried `resources/images/team/Max.jpeg` and `…/tobiu.png`, so the guard read its own test as the reference and those two frames stopped being unnamed — 420 became 418 without a single commit touching them. Renaming the fixtures to `fixtures/roster/Max-fixture.jpeg` restored 420.

Two consequences worth your judgement, both outside this PR: a rule whose key is the last two segments is named by *any* packed text file mentioning that pair, including a guard's own spec; and your follow-up idea — a text file in the image's own folder may name it by bare name — would enlarge that surface, since any file in that folder could then name every frame in it.

### RA-2 — one source for the extension sets

`IMAGE_ALTERNATIVES` and `TEXT_ALTERNATIVES` are derived from the two arrays and the three patterns are built from them, so adding `avif` to `IMAGE_EXTENSIONS` is now the only edit a new format needs. The arrays are no longer decorations.

### RA-3 — the claim now matches the code

You are right about the precedence: the condition takes whichever shape opens first, and a pretty-printed lifecycle object ahead of the payload makes `objectStart` 0 and `JSON.parse` throw on the array after it. The behaviour stays (throwing is the safe direction); the writing changed:

- docblock: the payload is the first line that opens an array **or** an object, npm 12 keys by package name while npm 11 and earlier report an array, and a lifecycle line that opens one of its own reds the gate;
- `@throws` and the error text say "no JSON array or object";
- the misleading case is renamed to *a one-line lifecycle object ahead of the payload does not take its place* (true: it never opens a line, so the array is still first), and a new case feeds exactly your string — `'{\n  "status": "completed"\n}\n[…'` — and asserts the throw.

### RA-4 — the reasons now say what happened

Verified through the API, since my clone is shallow and `6006fb2dc3` is not in it: the commit is `Docs App: remove the tutorials section #5383`, 2024-04-08, and it removed `docs/tutorials/*`. All four rows now read: *Orphaned since the Docs app's tutorials section was removed (`6006fb2dc3`, 2024-04-08, #5383). Kept because deleting a doc image is a content decision, not this guard's.*

One more commit on top of the four actions, because RA-1's own ratchet caught a bug in the change request it was answering.

### The baseline was naming the images it exempts

Pushed as `e54a671`, `baseline / guards` came back red with **8 stale entries** — every `path` row, while the 4 prefixes passed. The guard was right and my measurement was wrong: I had been checking against a `npm pack --json` report captured *before* the baseline existed. On CI the pack is fresh, the baseline file ships in it, and each row spells the image it exempts:

```
DIAG docs/resources/images/tutorials/create-app-choose-name.png packed=true
     unnamedInSet=false namers=["buildScripts/util/check-package-contents-baseline.json"]
```

So the exemption list was being read as evidence, naming every baselined frame and retiring every row. An exemption list is not a reference: `collectUnnamedImages` now takes `ignoredFiles`, defaulting to the baseline's own tarball path, and a spec case feeds a baseline body that spells its image and asserts the image is still reported unnamed. A second case keeps the other direction honest — an ordinary packed file still names its image.

This is the same lesson as your RA-1 in a different place: a guard that is measured against its own bookkeeping tells you what it already believes. It also means my earlier "420 unnamed, 0 added, 0 stale" was measured against a stale pack and proves nothing; the numbers below are from a pack that contains the baseline.

### 📋 Required Actions

To proceed with merging, please address the following:

- [ ] **RA-1: the baseline only fails upward.** An entry that no longer covers an unnamed packed image stays silently. Its file may have been deleted or renamed, it may now be named by folder and file name, or it may be a prefix that covers nothing. The list then drifts into things that used to be true. Every other entry baseline in `buildScripts/util/` fails on a stale entry for exactly this reason. I checked all five: `check-class-module-scope` (`diffAgainstBaseline` → `burnedDown`: "The ratchet is symmetric, following `check-engine-brain-boundary`"), `check-engine-brain-boundary`, `check-content-root-derivations` ("ratchets both ways"), `check-fixed-sleeps` ("in both directions") and `check-theme-value-files` (`[stale-baseline]`). Make such an entry fail the check with its own message. Removing the row in the same commit is the good direction. Cover both kinds in the spec: a `path` entry whose file is unpacked or now named, and a `prefix` entry that covers no unnamed image. (The ticket pointed at the sibling's JSON, while the ratchet lives in its script, so that gap is the ticket's, not yours.)
- [ ] **RA-2: two sources for the extension sets.** `IMAGE_EXTENSIONS` and `TEXT_EXTENSIONS` are exported and read nowhere: `git grep` at `a3865e6645` finds only their declarations. `IMAGE_PATTERN`, `IMAGE_TEST` and `TEXT_TEST` spell the same lists again as literals, so adding `avif` to the array changes nothing. Build the three patterns from the arrays, or drop the arrays.
- [ ] **RA-3: `parsePackOutput` states a precedence the code doesn't have.** The new comment says "The array wins when both are present", and the third new spec case is named for it. The condition actually takes whichever shape opens first.
